attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, describing his own 2019 book with Davis.

semantics.note: A past-tense description of the book's central argument. 'Such trust' points back to trustworthy and reliable AI, and the proposition ties it to the 2019 book and the approaches current then. Nothing is added or lost.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: the book presented prevailing approaches, mainly deep learning, as not enough for trustworthy AI and called for a change. It grades how he describes the book, not whether the book was technically right.

evidence.note: A 2019 InfoQ Q&A with Marcus and Davis named in the byline. The key takeaways are probably the authors' own framing, so this is the speaker describing his own book and can't independently confirm it. It is consistent with the claim.

An independent 2023 University of Tokyo book-club report, published before the evaluation date. It says the book argued that current deep-learning AI falls short and proposed a new strategy, and it tags the book with trustworthy AI and robustness. That fits the theme Marcus describes.

reviews.rationale: Marcus says the main point of Rebooting AI (2019) was that the approaches of the time weren't producing trustworthy AI. An independent account (e2) says the book argued that current deep-learning AI was insufficient and proposed a different strategy, and the subtitle, Building AI We Can Trust, fits. e1 is consistent but is largely the authors' own words, so it counts only as context. No counterevidence was found. The book itself wasn't checked, but the support condition is met.
